first-light.purpose: The paper. Set on html alone, never on body.

midnight-violet.purpose: The ink, and the foreground on every light surface.

frosted-heather.purpose: Seed for the todo state. Survives only in the rim and badge.

frosted-heather-tint.purpose: tintOf() at L*94, chroma capped 26. What a resting card is actually made of.

signal-amber.purpose: The doing state. The one seed the solver leaves untouched — already 7.3:1 on ink.

settled-green.purpose: Seed for the done state. Never painted.

settled-green-painted.purpose: What fill() resolves the seed to so white clears 5.5:1. The surface you actually see.

worst-case-backdrop.purpose: Pure black under a 60% scrim. Not paintable — it is what every contrast solve is run against.

session-violet.purpose: Chart fallback anchor before the solver runs. The last trace of the original fixed palette.

stale-red.purpose: The plan-age line when the sync has expired. The only warning colour in the system.

letterbox-black.purpose: Behind YouTube frames, so a loading video is a violet void rather than a grey box.

read-card.purpose: The single tonal step above paper. The whole depth vocabulary of the Read register.

read-ink.purpose: Body text and the masthead rule.

read-ink-3.purpose: Captions, week labels, axis, eyebrows. Raised from a 2.58:1 grey that looked right to a measured 4.59:1.

zone-easy.purpose: Coolest band of the intensity ramp.

zone-steady.purpose: Still cool: an easy week stays quiet.

zone-threshold.purpose: Warm. Visible from across the room.

zone-max.purpose: Hottest band. Only the top two zones are allowed to be warm.

display.purpose: Read-register masthead. Antonio 600, uppercase, on a 2px ink rule.

headline.purpose: The selected day's title in the Read register.

clock.purpose: The session timer. Largest element on screen, always — it is read from the floor, mid-hold.

title.purpose: An exercise name on a card.

body.purpose: Notes, verdicts and the prescription in Execute. Held to a 42ch measure.

prescription.purpose: Stryd's own prose, quoted pre-wrap in mono. Never restyled.

label.purpose: Every section heading. h2 and h3 are visually identical by design.

micro.purpose: Axis figures, week strips, eyebrows, step count.

shadows.name: rest
shadows.purpose: A lit top edge and the faintest possible anchor to the page. The default for a glass card.

shadows.name: doing
shadows.purpose: Tinted with the card's own amber. Paired with scale:1.015. Signals state, not height.

shadows.name: done
shadows.purpose: Tinted green with a dimmer inset — a finished card recedes.

shadows.name: inset-rim
shadows.purpose: A one-pixel highlight standing in for a border on translucent panels, chips and pills.

shadows.name: session-bar
shadows.purpose: Upward, separating the bar from the content it is deliberately not covering.

blurs.name: session-bar
blurs.purpose: The heaviest blur in the system — the bar must stay legible over anything at all.

motion.name: flip
motion.purpose: The card face swap. Replaced outright, not slowed, under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: bar-enter
motion.purpose: The session bar rising from translateY(100%).

motion.name: block-rise
motion.purpose: The Read block building itself once on arrival, from scaleY(.04).

motion.name: spotlight
motion.purpose: Everything that is not the active card receding toward the paper.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: translateY(2px). The single interaction physic in the app — there is no hover-lift.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Global. Not a degradation — the flip and the block are re-authored as static states.

dimTokens.name: --dim-o
dimTokens.purpose: Opacity of everything that is not the active card during a session.

dimTokens.name: --dim-bg-o
dimTokens.purpose: The backdrop photograph calms with them.

dimTokens.name: forced-colors reset
dimTokens.purpose: In forced colours the palette is the user's, and dimming it is not ours to do.

components.name: Phase Tabs
components.description: One phase on screen at a time, chosen from a scrolling strip rather than by folding four headers. A fold answers “what else is there” by making you open things; a strip answers it at a glance.

components.name: Session Bar
components.description: The signature component. A slim fixed bar, not a sheet — what the shape buys is the screen behind it, so the exercise being timed stays visible while the timer runs. Progress is the bar's own top edge. Glyphs are inline SVG inheriting currentColor, never the pause/next characters, which render as colour emoji on many Androids.

components.name: The Block
components.description: Six weeks of prescribed training as one row of columns: height is the day's load, the stacked fill is where that load was spent on the intensity ramp, a rest day is a dotted baseline rather than a gap. Dashed gridlines carry the scale, because a shape without a scale is decoration.

components.name: Intensity Legend
components.description: The Read register's key. Cool through hot, only the top two bands warm, so a hard day is visible from across the room.

narrative.overview:
Nothing in the Execute register is picked by eye. The palette is a seed of five authored colors and a set of solvers that derive every surface, rim, label and veil from them at boot, each one proven against the worst case the backdrop can produce — a pure black video frame under the thinnest part of the scrim. The identity of this system is that rigour. A card is amber because a movement is being done, and it is that amber because that is the lightest amber which still carries Midnight Violet at 7:1. The look is a consequence of the constraint, not a decoration applied over it.

The system runs in two deliberate registers, and they are allowed to look unrelated because they answer different questions in different rooms. Execute (index.html) is a phone held in a wet hand immediately after a run: glass panes float over a photograph, corners are generous (26px), type is heavy and short, and color carries exactly one meaning — what state a movement is in. Read (web/index.html) is a desk and a training block seen whole: ink on cool paper, zero radius, hairline rules, Antonio over IBM Plex, and color carries exactly one meaning — how hard the effort is.

What binds them is method, not appearance: contrast is solved rather than guessed (the Read register raises a caption grey from a measured 2.58:1 to 4.59:1 for exactly the same reason the Execute register runs a solver); color means one thing at a time; and every motion, transparency and forced-color preference is honoured rather than assumed.
keyCharacteristics: Two registers, one method — glass and runtime solving to execute, ink and print to read.
Color is a state channel, never an identity or a decoration.
Contrast is computed against a paranoid worst case, never eyeballed.
Depth reports state; it does not simulate height.
Every reduced-motion, reduced-transparency and forced-colors path is a designed state, not a fallback.
Legibility at arm's length, from the floor, mid-hold, wins every tie.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Within a register, hue answers exactly one question. In Execute that question is “what state is this movement in”; in Read it is “how hard is this”. A color introduced to distinguish, brand, or enliven anything is a defect, not a variation.

rules.name: The Worst-Case Rule
rules.body: No foreground colour is authored. Every one is derived by solver (inkFor, fade, fill) against Worst-Case Backdrop, not against the colour a surface appears to be. Adding a hand-picked hex to a glass surface bypasses the only thing keeping the app legible over arbitrary footage.

rules.name: The Quantised Check Rule
rules.body: Contrast is validated on the rounded 8-bit hex, never on the float. Rounding costs about 0.01 and was landing values at 4.4999 against a 4.5 target.

rules.name: The Floor-Read Rule
rules.body: The running clock is read from the floor, mid-hold, a couple of feet away. It is the one element allowed to consume height, and nothing may grow past it.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Size Rule
rules.body: Execute establishes hierarchy with weight (900 against 500) and tracking, not with a type scale. There are only four real sizes on a card — 19, 13.5, 12, 11 — and adding a fifth flattens the three that matter.

rules.name: The Ellipsis Rule
rules.body: Single-line elements in the session bar truncate; they never wrap. A long exercise name must not grow the bar and push the screen behind it out of view.

rules.name: The 620 Rule
rules.body: The Execute column never exceeds 620px, on any viewport. The flipped card's minimum height is derived from that number, so widening the column silently breaks the video frame — and where container queries are available the card measures itself with 100cqw instead of trusting the constant.

rules.name: The One Phase Rule
rules.body: Exactly one phase section is displayed at a time. Two open sections is not a denser layout, it is a lost tab strip.

rules.name: Shadow Is State, Not Height
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A shadow appears because a movement is being done or has been completed, and it is tinted with that state's own colour. A shadow added to signal importance, hierarchy, or hoverability is wrong here.

rules.name: The Spotlight Rule
rules.body: While a session runs, everything that is not the active card recedes toward the paper and the backdrop photograph calms with them. Dimming is done element by element, never with an overlay — these cards are glass, and a scrim laid behind them would be sampled by their own backdrop-filter, darkening the one card the spotlight exists to keep lit. Under forced-colors the dim tokens reset: the palette is the user's, and dimming it is not ours to do.

rules.name: The Two-Radius Rule
rules.body: A surface is either a 26px glass card or a 0px printed panel. Nothing in this system has an 8px corner. Choosing a radius means choosing a register.

rules.name: The Pill Rule
rules.body: If it can be pressed and it holds a word, it is a 99px pill. If it holds a glyph, it is a circle. Rectangular buttons exist only in the end-of-session prompt row, where the words would not fit a 34px circle.

dos: Do derive every foreground from a solver against Worst-Case Backdrop (#939199). inkFor for text on glass, fade for a secondary tone, fill for a surface that must carry a known foreground.
Do keep hue meaning one thing per register: state in Execute, intensity in Read.
Do tint state shadows with the surface's own solid (var(--solid)), never with black.
Do press with translateY(2px) over 120ms — the single interaction physic in the app.

Do write every prefers-reduced-motion, prefers-reduced-transparency and forced-colors branch as a designed state. Glass has no meaning in forced colours; those branches replace it with Canvas plus a CanvasText border, and mark active and done cards with Highlight and LinkText borders instead of fills.
Do ship a @supports not (backdrop-filter) path that falls back to opaque panels.
Do quote Stryd's prescription with pre-wrap and leave its own formatting intact.
Do keep small Read-register text at or above 4.59:1 — the measured value, not the one that looks right.
donts: Don't author a foreground hex on a glass surface. It bypasses the only thing keeping the app legible over arbitrary footage.
Don't colour anything by identity. Nine cards must never mean nine hues.

Don't introduce a dark theme, a neon accent, or a carbon-fibre texture. This is a light interface on pale paper; dimming during a session recedes toward the paper, and darkening it would invert the whole app for the length of a hold.
Don't add streaks, badges, confetti, closing rings or congratulatory copy. The app reports what happened.
Don't use an 8px radius. Pick a register.
Don't put a background on body — it paints over the negative-z-index backdrop.
Don't dim with an overlay. Glass samples what is behind it, so an overlay darkens the very card the spotlight exists to keep lit.
Don't let anything on the session bar wrap, or grow past the clock.
Don't add a hover-lift, a second press physic, or a shadow that signals importance rather than state.
Don't widen the Execute column past 620px without moving the flipped card's height derivation with it.
